_comment: SHARED busy / progress modal (scenes/shared/ — Aaron 2026-08-14 ruling 2A3592D0): the overlay a long operation (a bake, a scan, an import) puts up while it runs. The confirm.scene.json shape with a `resource_gauge` as the bar, exactly as Loading.scene.json draws its load bar. THE PROGRESS IS NOT PUBLISHED BY THE HOST SCENE: only the TOP scene updates, so a host frozen under this overlay could not feed it per frame — the fraction rides a SHARED handle (`ModalProgress`) the host hands over in its `ModalParams` and whatever is doing the work writes, and `SharedModal` reads it into `modal_progress` (0..1) every frame it is up. The same handle's done flag closes the modal. Cancel is the ONLY control and it is gated on `modal_cancellable`: an operation with nothing to abort shows a bar and no way to lie about stopping it. Esc / pad-B fold to `modal_cancel` via the root `on_cancel`, which the HOST always injects — whether that exit may be TAKEN is the popup_panel's own `dismissable` toggle, driven from `scripts/shared/busy.lua` (ruling DA0E1B57). NO `behaviour` key (the manifest skips scenes/shared/); this is the one param-driven tree WITH a pair script, because it is the one with a runtime behaviour of its own; chrome styles ride Main.scene.json's carrier through `main_scene_styles()`.

children._comment: THE DISMISSABLE TOGGLE (ruling DA0E1B57): `dismissable_bind` names the Model key `scripts/shared/busy.lua`'s arrange() publishes — `modal_cancellable or modal_done`. While it reads false the walker SWALLOWS Esc / pad-B for this screen, so a running operation with nothing to abort cannot be walked away from; it goes true the moment the caller offered a cancel or the work finished. NEVER author `dismissable: false` statically here (the registry gate forbids it): a static false is a trap the moment the Lua stops running, and the default is TRUE for exactly that reason.
